english_classification.chapter_title: The Chapter of the Man who asks: Why [am] I sometimes at peace, and troubled at other times?
english_classification.chapter_note: The chapter divides cleanly into an extended dialogue-frame question (¶1-5) and a cosmological teaching answer (¶6-11). The substrate teaching is distinctive: it maps psychic disturbance and peace to two cosmic mechanisms — (1) stellar/archontic influence via roots and birth-signs, and (2) the light/dark ratio in nourishment, including a transmigration doctrine about 'justified souls' whose 'dues have ceased' entering through food. Both mechanisms stay entirely within the cosmic system. Gardner flags the 'dues have ceased' passage as potentially Buddhist-influenced (karmic consequences). The dialogue frame is unusually elaborate — three paragraphs describing the disciple's experiential states. ¶4 introduces Manichaean institutional practices (fasting, psalms, prayer) into the question. The seam flag on ¶11 is a false positive — the paragraph recaps substrate conduit-teaching without institutional application. Negative editorial fatigue score and increasing substrate density in the second half confirm the teaching core is concentrated in ¶6-11.
